rulesNotes: This is the general Criminal Justice program for the selected delivery format. Concentrations have different requirements and must not inherit this ledger without review.

At least 30 credits must be earned through Liberty and at least 30 must be upper level. The 90-credit outside maximum is a ceiling, not a claim that this draft identifies 90 applicable outside credits.

The catalog requires 25% of the major at Liberty. This model conservatively uses all 45 foundation/core hours and reserves 12 hours rounded to three-credit courses; Liberty must confirm its exact major-residency denominator.
GOVT 220 fills both the foundation requirement and cultural studies; it is one course and three credits, never six. GOVT 200 is not reused for critical thinking.
Receiving Liberty course level controls upper-level counting. A source course with an advanced number does not itself establish an upper-level award.
Options within a requirement are alternatives; choosing multiple alternatives does not create extra applicable credits.
Approved transfer totals of 45 may waive RLGN 105 and EVAN 101; approved totals of 60 may also waive THEO 201 and THEO 202. Waivers are not automatic and award no credit.
If Liberty approves a requirement waiver or technology/UNIV exemption, add nonduplicating degree-applicable elective credit to preserve 120 hours. This baseline does not apply those waivers.
Outside mappings not found for exact major requirements remain research gaps. Their university fallbacks do not establish that Liberty requires those courses in residence.

University major prerequisite pairs are modeled; other university elective/general-education prerequisites, provider prerequisites and actual course offerings require review. No finish date is verified.

unresolved.message: Submit official learning records for Liberty’s individual transfer evaluation; personal acceptance, duplicate learning and catalog eligibility depend on those records.
The current provider recommendation version and recommendation window still need review for any selected outside option without that evidence.

The baseline allocates 45 major credits once. The existing 25% major-residency fraction equals 11.25 credits; the model conservatively retains at least 12 credits through whole three-credit Liberty major courses.
Additional outside awards can improve this route. The existing named university choices remain valid baseline courses; their presence does not establish that outside credit is disallowed.

This 120-credit baseline retains the listed religion and introductory technology requirements. It applies no transfer-triggered religion, technology or UNIV waiver and awards no assumed replacement-elective credit.
If a personal transfer award qualifies for a waiver, have Liberty apply the waiver and approve nonduplicating replacement electives before changing this retained baseline.
The selected university courses still need exact source-bound prerequisite review where the baseline retains a generic scheduling note.

Before registering, check available sections, accepted prerequisite credit and transcript deadlines. The reviewed CJUS 420 catalog block lists a fall offering; this baseline does not establish an executable finish date.

The current residential guide publishes two distinct one-credit source courses and receiving elective subjects. The catalog permits the same course to count only once; this fresh baseline uses each named source course once.
Include prior coursework and exam awards in Liberty’s individual transfer evaluation so the same course is not counted twice. This baseline does not clear a conflict with an unknown prior record.
If a one-credit university fallback is selected, choose an actual named course for that requirement.
